**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT, § 11.3 Suspected Violations).**

- The only Customer-facing examination right in the Agreement is IBM's right in § 11.3 (p0132) to investigate potential violations of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b). No audit/inspection/verification clause exists elsewhere (searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "monitor" returned nothing relevant; §§ 11.5 and 13.2 add no monitoring rights).
- As drafted the right is unlimited in frequency and unannounced — the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt and applies solely before IBM restricts access or removes Content — with no cost allocation, no confidentiality obligation on investigators and no exclusion of access to our systems. That fails the fallback on all material terms.
- Redline (validated, ok:true) inserts the fallback guardrails into p0132: once per twelve months, 15 days' prior written notice, business hours, independent investigator under confidentiality, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%, and no direct or remote access to our systems or Customer Components. We chose the fallback over the preferred 30-day/5% formulation because a 30-day wait would be disproportionate where IBM suspects unlawful Content on its hosted infrastructure.
